newsitem.title: USA: IXC makes fiber-optic network route swap.
newsitem.headline: IXC makes fiber-optic network route swap.

text.p: IXC Communications Inc said Thursday it had an agreement with Vyvx, Inc to trade rights to use fiber on new and future network routes.

The company described the agreement as a strategic move that further extends the reach of its coast-to-coast digital Fiber optic network into the Southeastern United States, The agreement will reduce IXC's, construction costs on the second phase of its expansion program by more than $100 million.

The agreement gives IXC the competitive advantage of a lower cost structure, enabling the company to apply funds earmarked for this project to future network expansions. It also allows IXC to expand its network capabilities faster and more efficiently than originally planned.

IXC will exchange rights to use dark fiber, without optionics, along its New York-to-Los Angeles route for rights to use dark fiber on the Washington, D.C.-to-Houston route that Vyvx will begin building in 1997. Construction of the route is expected to be completed quickly because Vyvx has existing relationships with the pipeline subsidiaries of its parent company, The Williams Companies, which owns rights of way.

For IXC customers, this expansion will mean greater network access and more points of presence in a region that is a significant and growing long distance market. This new route will begin in Washington, D.C., and continue through Richmond, Va.; Greensboro, Winston-Salem and Charlotte, N.C.; Greenville, S.C.; Atlanta; Birmingham and Montgomery, Ala.; Hattiesburg and Meridian, Miss.; and Baton Rouge La., ending in Houston.

IXC provides capacity on its digital fiber network to regional long distance carriers, local telephone companies, cable companies, Internet access providers and other value-added carriers that offer telecommunications services to residential and commercial customers. The company is undergoing a major network expansion of more than 7,000 miles, incorporating the most advanced transmission technology available. The 1,600 miles from Vyvx are scheduled to be completed during the next year.

Vyvx is a provider of integrated fiber-optic, satellite and teleport video transmission services. It is the international video communications unit of the WilTech Group Inc, one of the Williams Cos Inc, in Tulsa, Okla.
